title: The electric telegraph
summary: William Fothergill Cooke and Charles Wheatstone patented the electric telegraph in 1837, developing it for Britain's new railways. In the United States, Samuel Morse opened a government-funded line from Baltimore to Washington in 1844. Delegates met at the first International Telegraph Conference in Paris in 1865. A transatlantic cable laid in 1866 lasted, and by the early 1870s cables reached India, Australia, East Asia and South America, nearly all built by British firms. Soon almost every major city joined the global network.
